newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt roars higher, may eye more records.
newsitem.headline: German debt roars higher, may eye more records.

text.p: The German bond market, fresh from roaring to an all-time record high in London earlier on Wednesday morning, looks poised to storm still higher as investors need to place excess cash.
"The mood continues to be very optimistic and there is still enough liquidity with people looking for places to invest it," said on trader predicting the market's heady days are not over yet.
"Everyone believes the market cannot fall because there is still a lot of liquidity out there," added another trader.

Although profit-taking helped pull the market off its morning highs, the December Bund futures contract, traded on Frankfurt's DTB exchange, still closed up four basis points at 101.37. In London the contract was up one basis point at 101.38 in late trading, having come off its all-time high of 101.56.
The April 2006 cash bond traded at 103.21, down from its 103.25 close on Tuesday.
But some dealers were slightly more sceptical saying upward moves would be limited as many banks had already closed their books for the year and were not interested in taking on new positions.
"There is just day to day trading," a dealer said.
Dealers predicted activity would be slowed on Thursday as the market lacks the usual trading impulses from the U.S. markets, which will be closed to celebrate Thanksgiving on Thursday.
The Friday after Thanksgiving, when dealings in the U.S. are traditionally slow, may also see lower than usual volumes in Europe, dealers said.
